title: Intrinsic Motivation and Achievement in Mathematics in Elementary School archgate.net/publication/282135309_Intrinsic_motivation_and_achievement_in_mathematics_in_elem
author: Barton, Craig
source: Tips for Teachers (tipsforteachers.co.uk), January 9, 2025 — original paper: https://www.rese
summary: Barton covers Garon-Carrier et al.'s longitudinal study tracking 1,478 Canadian children across grades 1 to 4, using cross-lagged models to test the direction of the relationship between intrinsic motivation and mathematics achievement. The finding runs against the conventional classroom assumption: prior achievement significantly predicts later intrinsic motivation, but motivation does not significantly predict later achievement. The pattern held regardless of gender, and math achievement itself proved highly stable across the early primary years, while intrinsic motivation was more changeable — especially around school entry — before stabilizing under achievement's influence. Barton draws the practical implication that teachers chasing math achievement through motivation-boosting interventions may be pulling the wrong lever; the study suggests engineering early experiences of genuine success is what more reliably builds motivation, not the reverse.
points: Prior mathematics achievement predicts later intrinsic motivation, but intrinsic motivation does not significantly predict later achievement — the causal arrow runs the opposite way from common classroom assumptions.

A student's level of maths achievement is fairly well established early in primary school, making early intervention and assessment of numeracy skills disproportionately important for long-term trajectory.

Autonomy-promoting interventions aimed at boosting intrinsic motivation may not be the most effective lever in the early school years, since motivation appears to follow achievement rather than drive it at this stage.

Individual differences in maths achievement are highly stable over time, while intrinsic motivation is more volatile early on and becomes more stable only as it settles under the influence of prior achievement.
quotes: Contrary to the hypothesis that intrinsic motivation drives achievement or that motivation and achievement entertain reciprocal influences over time, it is rather achievement that predicts later intrinsic motivation in mathematics during the primary school years
The study found that prior achievement in mathematics predicts later intrinsic motivation in mathematics, but not the reverse.
The study indicates that a student's level of achievement in mathematics is fairly well established early in primary school and predicts later motivation.

The study found that individual differences in math achievement were highly stable, while intrinsic motivation was more likely to change at school entry, becoming more stable later due to previous achievement.

This suggests that rather than focusing primarily on fostering intrinsic motivation as a means to improve math achievement, teachers should focus on creating opportunities for students to experience success in mathematics.
